reuse: Monday's $4.99/lb pork does two nights. Roast all 4 tenderloins on Monday: 2 get the honey garlic glaze, and 2 stay plain and go into Wednesday's noodle bowls, so Wednesday needs no raw meat. Monday also makes Wednesday's pickled carrots, which need 2 hours, while the oven runs. Wednesday makes Thursday's chimichurri so it can rest overnight, and the same chimichurri dresses Thursday's salad. Shared produce: limes and cilantro (Tue + Wed), hot house cucumbers and romaine (Wed + Thu), Campari tomatoes (Tue + Thu), and jalapeños on the side (Tue + Wed). Deals behind the menu: pork tenderloin $4.99/lb, P&D white shrimp 24 oz $13.49, inside skirt steak $11.99/lb.

dinners.name: Honey Garlic Pork Tenderloin with Jasmine Rice & Roasted Broccoli
dinners.blurb: THE DEAL: Publix extra lean pork tenderloin, $4.99/lb, the best protein value in this week's ad. Seared pork glazed in a sticky honey garlic and cider vinegar sauce, with charred broccoli and jasmine rice.
dinners.warn: COOK ONCE, EAT TWICE: roast all 4 tenderloins. Glaze 2 for tonight and leave 2 plain for Wednesday. Make Wednesday's pickled carrots first. TONIGHT: move one shrimp bag to the fridge to thaw for Tuesday.
dinners.alt: Sliced pork tenderloin glazed with a glossy honey garlic sauce in a skillet

items: Rub, doubled to cover all 4: 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp black pepper

ingredients.group: Honey garlic sauce (as written, for tonight's 2)

items: 4 large carrots, cut into thin batons

directions: About 5:00, make Wednesday's pickles: stir the sugar and salt into 1 1/2 cups boiling water until dissolved, add the rice vinegar, and drop in the carrot batons so they're just covered. Cool, cover and refrigerate for Wednesday.
Start the jasmine rice. Heat the oven to 350°F.
Toss the broccoli with 2 Tbsp oil, salt and pepper on a sheet pan and put it on the lower rack. It roasts about 25 min while the pork cooks.
Stir the cider vinegar, soy sauce and honey together in a bowl. Mix the rub and rub it all over the 4 tenderloins.

Heat 1 1/2 Tbsp oil in a large ovenproof skillet over high heat. Sear 2 tenderloins (tonight's) until golden on all sides, about 5 min. Push them to one side, add the garlic and cook until golden. Pour in the sauce, turn the pork once, and put the skillet in the oven.
Sear the other 2 tenderloins in a second pan with the remaining 1 1/2 Tbsp oil. Put them on a sheet pan with NO sauce and into the oven alongside.
Roast 15-18 min, until the center reads 155°F (the recipe's target; 145°F is safe if you like it pinker).

Rest tonight's pork on a plate under loose foil for 5 min. Broil the broccoli 2 min for char. Simmer the skillet sauce over medium-high about 3 min, until it's a thin syrup. Return the pork, turn it to coat, and slice it thick. Serve with rice, broccoli and extra sauce.
Cool the 2 plain tenderloins, wrap them whole (unsliced stays juicier), and refrigerate for Wednesday. Move one bag of shrimp to the fridge for Tuesday.
dinners.reuse: Makes Wednesday's protein (2 plain tenderloins) and Wednesday's pickled carrots.

dinners.name: Shrimp Fajitas with Flour Tortillas, Avocado & Lime Yogurt
dinners.blurb: THE DEAL: Publix peeled & deveined white shrimp, large, 24 oz, $13.49 (about $9/lb), plus BOGO La Banderita flour tortillas and BOGO Florida avocados. Cumin-chili shrimp seared hard, with blistered peppers and onions. Fastest night of the week.
dinners.warn: Recipe scaled 2x (2 lb shrimp) so Paul gets about 8 oz. Cook in 2 batches so the shrimp sear instead of steaming. FLOUR tortillas only. The recipe card allows corn, and Gina won't eat corn.
dinners.alt: Shrimp fajitas with peppers and onions in flour tortillas with avocado and cilantro

items: 2 lb large shrimp, peeled, deveined, tails off, thawed (bag 1 + 8 oz of bag 2)
1/2 tsp chipotle chile powder, divided (recipe uses 1 tsp at 2x; halved for the kids)
2 red/organic bell peppers + 2 green bell peppers, in 1/4-inch strips
2 yellow onions, halved and sliced 1/4 inch
1 cup plain Greek yogurt (stir in a squeeze of lime)
Sliced jalapeño and hot sauce on the side

directions: Pat the shrimp dry. Toss them in a big bowl with 1 Tbsp oil, 2 tsp cumin, 1 tsp chili powder, 1/4 tsp chipotle and 1 tsp salt. Zest both limes over the bowl and toss again.
Wrap the tortillas in foil and warm them in a 300°F oven.

Heat 1 Tbsp oil in your largest skillet over medium-high. Add half the peppers and onions with half the remaining cumin, chili powder, chipotle and salt. Cook 6-8 min, until soft and browned in spots. Stir in half the garlic for 30 seconds, then move to a platter. Repeat with the second half (1 Tbsp oil).

Add 1 Tbsp oil and heat until shimmering. Spread half the shrimp in one layer and sear about 3 min total, until opaque and curled into a C. Don't overcook. Repeat with the last 1 Tbsp oil and the remaining shrimp.
Pile the shrimp on the platter with the vegetables and squeeze the lime juice over everything.
Serve with warm flour tortillas, avocado, lime yogurt, feta, tomato and cilantro. Jalapeño and hot sauce go on the side.
dinners.reuse: Shares cilantro, limes and jalapeños with Wed, and a Campari tomato pack with Thu. The second avocado stays whole for Wednesday. The leftover 1 lb of shrimp stays in the freezer.

dinners.name: Vietnamese Pork Noodle Bowls with Pickled Carrots & Nuoc Cham
dinners.blurb: THE DEAL: no new protein. It uses Monday's $4.99/lb tenderloin, plus DEAL hot house cucumbers 3/$5. Cool rice noodles, crunchy lettuce and cucumber, Monday's pickles, mint, cilantro and peanuts, with charred sliced pork and a bright fish sauce-lime dressing.
dinners.warn: Uses Monday's 2 plain tenderloins in place of the recipe's overnight lemongrass pork. BEAN SPROUTS LEFT OUT (no-beans rule). Use rice vermicelli, not bean-thread noodles. AFTER DINNER: make Thursday's chimichurri (5 min).
dinners.alt: Vietnamese noodle bowl with sliced pork, rice vermicelli, pickled carrots, lettuce and herbs

items: Monday's 2 plain roasted tenderloins (about 1.5 lb cooked)
About 12 oz dried rice vermicelli (recipe's 7 oz, upsized for appetites)
1 hot house cucumber, halved and sliced on the diagonal
A big handful each of mint and cilantro
Sliced jalapeño or sriracha on the side
Chili left out of the sauce; serve it on the side

directions: Stir the nuoc cham ingredients together until the sugar dissolves.
Soak the vermicelli in boiling water about 5 min (or per the packet). Drain, rinse under cold water, and drain well.
Tear the romaine, slice the cucumber, pick the herbs, chop the peanuts, and drain the pickles.
Slice the pork thin and toss it with 2 Tbsp of the nuoc cham. Sear in 1 Tbsp oil in a very hot skillet, 1-2 min per side, just until the edges char and it's warm.
Build the bowls: noodles, lettuce, pickles, cucumber, pork, herbs, peanuts and a lime wedge. Pour nuoc cham over generously at the table.
After dinner, make Thursday's chimichurri (see Thursday) so it rests overnight.
dinners.reuse: Takes Monday's pork and pickles. Shares cilantro and limes with Tue, and cucumber and romaine with Thu. Makes Thursday's chimichurri tonight.

dinners.name: Skirt Steak with Chimichurri, Crispy Gold Potatoes & Cucumber-Tomato Salad
dinners.blurb: THE DEAL: Publix inside skirt steak, $11.99/lb, plus the 5-lb gold potato bag for $4.99 and BOGO Campari tomatoes. Hard-seared skirt steak sliced thin under a punchy garlic-parsley chimichurri, with crispy potatoes and a crunchy salad.
dinners.warn: 2.5 lb steak (recipe's 1.4 lb serves 4 small appetites). Chimichurri made 1.5x and should be made Wednesday night. Take the steak out of the fridge 30 min before cooking.
dinners.alt: Sliced seared steak topped with green chimichurri sauce

items: 1 bunch flat-leaf parsley (about 1 1/2 cups packed leaves)
Red pepper flakes on the side (recipe's 0-2 tsp, left out for the kids)
2.5 lb inside skirt steak, cut into 4-5 pieces to fit the pan
3 lb gold potatoes, halved or quartered
1 romaine heart, 1 hot house cucumber, 1 lb Campari tomatoes, for the salad

directions: (Wed night) Chop the parsley fine with the garlic, by hand or pulsing in a food processor (not pureed). Stir in the vinegar, salt, pepper and olive oil. Cover and refrigerate. Rest at least 1 hour; overnight is better.
About 5:00, take the steak out of the fridge. Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the potatoes with oil, salt and pepper and roast 35-40 min, flipping halfway, until crisp.
Chop the romaine, cucumber and tomatoes for the salad. Dress just before serving with 2-3 Tbsp chimichurri and a pinch of salt.
Heat a heavy skillet with the oil over high until it smokes. Season the steak generously with salt and pepper on both sides.
Cook in batches, about 2 min per side for medium-rare (125°F) or 2.5 min for medium (135°F), for steak about 3/4 inch thick.
Rest the steak 5-10 min under loose foil, then slice thinly AGAINST the grain.
Toss the hot potatoes with a spoonful of chimichurri. Serve the steak with the rest of the chimichurri, the potatoes and the salad. Pepper flakes go on the side.
dinners.reuse: Chimichurri doubles as the salad dressing and the potato toss. Shares cucumber and romaine with Wed, and Campari tomatoes with Tue.
